## Summary of findings

This report examines **nine TCRs (74, 79, 80, 81, 83, 84, 85, 89, and 90)** using their observed, paired **TRA and TRB 10x assembled contig sequences**. It addresses two questions: (1) what full assembled sequences are available, and (2) which candidate IMGT allele is better supported where the V/J gene annotation is ambiguous.

**Key results**

- **Sequence extraction:** One representative, observed same-cell TRA/TRB pair is selected for each of the nine TCRs using the quality and ranking criteria described in Question 1. These are assembled contigs, **not independently validated transduction constructs**.
- **Allele comparison:** There are **12 ambiguous chain/gene assignments** across the nine TCRs. Each is compared with **two IMGT candidate alleles** (24 contig-to-reference alignments in total).
- **Interpretation:** The favored allele is the one matching the observed contig at more **allele-discriminating nucleotide positions**. Orange highlights indicate nucleotide mismatches; pink indicates alignment gaps.

|---:|:---|:---|:---|:---|
| 74 | TRA | TRAV14/DV4 | TRAV14/DV4*01 | 3 vs 0 |
| 79 | TRB | TRBV7-2 | TRBV7-2*02 | 2 vs 0 |
| 80 | TRB | TRBV7-9 | TRBV7-9*01 | 1 vs 0 |
| 81 | TRA | TRAJ13 | TRAJ13*02 | 1 vs 0 |
| 81 | TRB | TRBV19 | TRBV19*01 | 2 vs 0 |
| 83 | TRB | TRBV7-9 | TRBV7-9*03 | 1 vs 0 |
| 84 | TRA | TRAJ13 | TRAJ13*02 | 1 vs 0 |
| 85 | TRA | TRAJ13 | TRAJ13*02 | 1 vs 0 |
| 85 | TRB | TRBV19 | TRBV19*01 | 2 vs 0 |

| 90 | TRA | TRAJ13 | TRAJ13*02 | 1 vs 0 |

*These are the candidate preferences from the current analysis. The detailed evidence tables and colored nucleotide alignments below allow each call to be checked against the underlying contig sequence.*

## Question 1. Can you share the full sequences for these nine TCRs?

**Answer:** Yes. The table below is generated directly from the original 10x assembled contig FASTA. Each of the nine TCRs is represented by one observed same-cell TRA/TRB pair. These are the **full available assembled contig sequences**, not independently verified complete transduction constructs.

### Input files

**Answer:** This report reads the three **original input files** directly. It does **not** require a previously generated sequence CSV.

| Original file | What it supplies |
|---|---|
| `TCR_top10_VDJ_annotations_by_donor_ambiguous.csv` | TCR IDs and their associated TRA/TRB contig IDs |
| `filtered_contig_annotations.csv` | Sample, cell barcode, chain, quality flags, UMIs, V/J genes |
| `filtered_contig.fasta` | Actual assembled nucleotide sequences |

Place these three files in the **same folder as this QMD** and render it. The extraction runs automatically.

```{r}
required <- c("TCR_top10_VDJ_annotations_by_donor_ambiguous.csv",
              "filtered_contig_annotations.csv", "filtered_contig.fasta")
missing <- required[!file.exists(required)]
if (length(missing)) stop("Missing original input(s) in working directory: ",
                          paste(missing, collapse=", "),
                          "\nPlace the 3 original files beside this QMD.")
map <- read.csv(required[1], check.names=FALSE, stringsAsFactors=FALSE)
ann <- read.csv(required[2], check.names=FALSE, stringsAsFactors=FALSE)
ids <- c(74,79,80,81,83,84,85,89,90)
stopifnot(all(c("TCR ID","donor","TRA_contig_id","TRB_contig_id") %in% names(map)))
stopifnot(all(c("sample","barcode","contig_id","chain","is_cell",
                "high_confidence","full_length","productive","umis",
                "v_gene","j_gene") %in% names(ann)))
map <- map[map[["TCR ID"]] %in% ids, ]
if (anyDuplicated(map[["TCR ID"]]) || nrow(map)!=length(ids))
  stop("Expected exactly one mapping row for each of the nine TCR IDs.")
ann$umis <- suppressWarnings(as.numeric(ann$umis))
ann$barcode <- as.character(ann$barcode)
ann$sample <- as.character(ann$sample)
ann$contig_id <- as.character(ann$contig_id)
# Read original FASTA without requiring Bioconductor packages.
fa <- readLines(required[3], warn=FALSE)
headers <- which(startsWith(fa, ">"))
if (!length(headers)) stop("No FASTA records found.")
ends <- c(headers[-1]-1L, length(fa))
fasta_ids <- sub("^>([^[:space:]]+).*", "\\1", fa[headers])
fasta_seqs <- vapply(seq_along(headers), function(i) {
  paste(fa[seq.int(headers[i]+1L, ends[i])], collapse="")
}, character(1))
if (anyDuplicated(fasta_ids)) stop("Duplicate contig IDs in FASTA.")
seq_by_id <- setNames(toupper(fasta_seqs), fasta_ids)
split_ids <- function(x) {
  if (is.na(x) || !nzchar(x)) return(character())
  trimws(strsplit(x, ";", fixed=TRUE)[[1]])
}
as_flag <- function(x) tolower(as.character(x)) %in% c("true","t","1")
```

### How the representative sequences were selected

**Answer:** For each TCR, we locate its listed TRA and TRB contigs in the original annotation CSV, attach the exact nucleotide strings from the original FASTA, and match **sample + barcode** to find both chains in the **same cell**.

Only pairs with **is_cell, high_confidence, full_length, and productive** true for **both chains** are eligible. Among eligible pairs, we rank the **exact TRA+TRB nucleotide pair** by the number of supporting cells, then combined UMIs, then sequence length. We choose an **observed pair**, never a synthetic consensus.

```{r}
results <- list()
audit <- list()
for (tcr in ids) {
  row <- map[map[["TCR ID"]]==tcr, , drop=FALSE]
  tra_ids <- split_ids(row$TRA_contig_id[1])
  trb_ids <- split_ids(row$TRB_contig_id[1])
  a <- ann[ann$contig_id %in% tra_ids & ann$chain=="TRA", , drop=FALSE]
  b <- ann[ann$contig_id %in% trb_ids & ann$chain=="TRB", , drop=FALSE]
  if (!nrow(a) || !nrow(b))
    stop("TCR ", tcr, ": no mapped TRA or TRB contigs in annotation CSV.")
  a$sequence_nt <- unname(seq_by_id[a$contig_id])
  b$sequence_nt <- unname(seq_by_id[b$contig_id])
  if (anyNA(a$sequence_nt) || anyNA(b$sequence_nt))
    stop("TCR ",tcr,": mapped contig missing from original FASTA.")
  a <- a[!duplicated(a$contig_id), , drop=FALSE]
  b <- b[!duplicated(b$contig_id), , drop=FALSE]
  pair <- merge(a, b, by=c("sample","barcode"), suffixes=c("_TRA","_TRB"))
  if (!nrow(pair)) stop("TCR ",tcr,": no TRA/TRB contigs observed in same cell.")
  qc_fields <- c("is_cell","high_confidence","full_length","productive")
  pair$both_QC_pass <- Reduce(`&`, lapply(qc_fields, function(n)
    as_flag(pair[[paste0(n,"_TRA")]]) &
    as_flag(pair[[paste0(n,"_TRB")]])))
  eligible <- pair[pair$both_QC_pass, , drop=FALSE]
  if (!nrow(eligible))
    stop("TCR ",tcr,": no same-cell pair passes all four QC flags; manual review required.")
  # Count distinct cells supporting each exact nucleotide TRA+TRB pair.
  eligible$exact_pair_key <- paste(eligible$sequence_nt_TRA,
                                   eligible$sequence_nt_TRB, sep="|")
  eligible$cell_key <- paste(eligible$sample, eligible$barcode, sep="|")
  support <- tapply(eligible$cell_key, eligible$exact_pair_key,
                    function(z) length(unique(z)))
  eligible$supporting_cells_same_exact_pair <-
    as.integer(support[eligible$exact_pair_key])
  eligible$combined_UMIs <- eligible$umis_TRA + eligible$umis_TRB
  eligible$combined_length <- nchar(eligible$sequence_nt_TRA) +
                              nchar(eligible$sequence_nt_TRB)
  eligible <- eligible[order(-eligible$supporting_cells_same_exact_pair,
                             -eligible$combined_UMIs,
                             -eligible$combined_length,
                             eligible$sample, eligible$barcode,
                             eligible$contig_id_TRA,
                             eligible$contig_id_TRB), , drop=FALSE]
  best <- eligible[1, , drop=FALSE]
  results[[as.character(tcr)]] <- data.frame(
    TCR_ID=tcr, donor=row$donor[1],
    sample=best$sample, barcode=best$barcode,
    TRA_sequence_nt=best$sequence_nt_TRA,
    TRB_sequence_nt=best$sequence_nt_TRB,
    TRA_contig_id=best$contig_id_TRA,
    TRB_contig_id=best$contig_id_TRB,
    TRA_v_gene=best$v_gene_TRA, TRA_j_gene=best$j_gene_TRA,
    TRB_v_gene=best$v_gene_TRB, TRB_j_gene=best$j_gene_TRB,
    TRA_UMIs=best$umis_TRA, TRB_UMIs=best$umis_TRB,
    QC_paired_cells=length(unique(eligible$cell_key)),
    supporting_cells_same_exact_pair=best$supporting_cells_same_exact_pair,
    TRA_unique_assembled_sequences=length(unique(a$sequence_nt)),
    TRB_unique_assembled_sequences=length(unique(b$sequence_nt)),
    sequence_source="filtered_contig.fasta",
    annotation_source="filtered_contig_annotations.csv",
    TCR_mapping_source="TCR_top10_VDJ_annotations_by_donor_ambiguous.csv",
    stringsAsFactors=FALSE
  )
  audit[[as.character(tcr)]] <- data.frame(
    TCR_ID=tcr, mapped_TRA_contigs=nrow(a), mapped_TRB_contigs=nrow(b),
    same_cell_candidate_pairs=nrow(pair),
    QC_pass_candidate_pairs=nrow(eligible),
    QC_paired_cells=length(unique(eligible$cell_key))
  )
}
x <- do.call(rbind, results)
audit_table <- do.call(rbind, audit)
rownames(x) <- NULL
stopifnot(nrow(x)==9, !anyDuplicated(x$TCR_ID),
          all(nzchar(x$TRA_sequence_nt)), all(nzchar(x$TRB_sequence_nt)))
write.csv(x, "TCR9_extracted_same_cell_TRA_TRB.csv", row.names=FALSE, na="")
write.csv(audit_table, "TCR9_extraction_audit.csv", row.names=FALSE)
```


### Full nucleotide sequences — one TRA/TRB pair per TCR

**Answer:** Exactly **nine rows**, one TCR per row. Each contains the unmodified observed TRA and TRB assembled nucleotide strings from `filtered_contig.fasta`.

```{r}
knitr::kable(x[,c("TCR_ID","TRA_sequence_nt","TRB_sequence_nt")],
             row.names=FALSE)
```

### Sequence provenance

**Answer:** Each selected TRA/TRB pair has the **same sample and barcode**. The exact contig IDs below identify the corresponding FASTA records.

```{r}
knitr::kable(x[,c("TCR_ID","donor","sample","barcode",
                  "TRA_contig_id","TRB_contig_id",
                  "TRA_UMIs","TRB_UMIs",
                  "supporting_cells_same_exact_pair")], row.names=FALSE)
```


## Question 2. Is there a way to resolve the ambiguities? Some ambiguities lead to amino acid differences in antigen-contacting loops.

**Answer:** Align each candidate IMGT allele to the **observed representative contig**, then examine nucleotide positions that distinguish the two alleles. The tables below are **calculated directly from those alignments**, not copied from a previous allele-call CSV.

**Additional input:** `IMGT_candidate_alleles.fasta` (the ten candidate allele reference sequences). This section requires the R packages `Biostrings` and `pwalign`; install once using `BiocManager::install(c("Biostrings", "pwalign"))`.

```{r}
if (!requireNamespace("Biostrings", quietly=TRUE) ||
    !requireNamespace("pwalign", quietly=TRUE))
  stop("Question 2 needs Biostrings and pwalign. Install with BiocManager::install(c('Biostrings','pwalign')).")
if (!file.exists("IMGT_candidate_alleles.fasta"))
  stop("Place IMGT_candidate_alleles.fasta beside this QMD.")
ref_lines <- readLines("IMGT_candidate_alleles.fasta", warn=FALSE)
rh <- which(startsWith(ref_lines, ">"))
re <- c(rh[-1]-1L, length(ref_lines))
rn <- sub("^>([^[:space:]]+).*", "\\1", ref_lines[rh])
refs <- setNames(vapply(seq_along(rh), function(i)
  toupper(paste(ref_lines[seq.int(rh[i]+1L,re[i])],collapse="")),
  character(1)), rn)
spec <- data.frame(
  TCR_ID=c(74,79,80,81,81,83,84,85,85,89,90,90),
  chain=c("TRA","TRB","TRB","TRA","TRB","TRB","TRA","TRA","TRB","TRA","TRA","TRB"),
  gene=c("TRAV14/DV4","TRBV7-2","TRBV7-9","TRAJ13","TRBV19",
         "TRBV7-9","TRAJ13","TRAJ13","TRBV19","TRAV14/DV4","TRAJ13","TRBV19"),
  stringsAsFactors=FALSE)
matrix_nt <- Biostrings::nucleotideSubstitutionMatrix(match=2,mismatch=-3,baseOnly=TRUE)
align_nt <- function(query, subject, type="local") {
  pwalign::pairwiseAlignment(
    Biostrings::DNAString(query),Biostrings::DNAString(subject),
    type=type,substitutionMatrix=matrix_nt,gapOpening=8,gapExtension=2)
}
chars <- function(z) strsplit(as.character(z),"",fixed=TRUE)[[1]]
# Translate alignment columns into reference coordinates. The aligned reference
# substring must have a unique placement in the original reference.
reference_map <- function(aln, full_ref) {
  q <- chars(pwalign::pattern(aln))
  r <- chars(pwalign::subject(aln))
  stopifnot(length(q)==length(r))
  ref_span <- paste0(r[r!="-"],collapse="")
  offsets <- gregexpr(ref_span,full_ref,fixed=TRUE)[[1]]
  if (offsets[1]<0 || length(offsets)!=1)
    stop("Reference alignment span cannot be placed uniquely.")
  rp <- offsets[1]-1L
  qp <- 0L
  out <- vector("list",length(q))
  n <- 0L
  for (i in seq_along(q)) {
    if (r[i]!="-") rp <- rp+1L
    if (q[i]!="-") qp <- qp+1L
    if (r[i]!="-") {
      n <- n+1L
      out[[n]] <- data.frame(ref_pos=rp, observed=q[i],
                             contig_alignment_pos=if(q[i]=="-") NA_integer_ else qp)
    }
  }
  do.call(rbind,out[seq_len(n)])
}
# Align the two IMGT alleles to identify discriminating reference positions.
reference_diffs <- function(a,b) {
  aln <- align_nt(a,b,"global")
  aa <- chars(pwalign::pattern(aln))
  bb <- chars(pwalign::subject(aln))
  i <- 0L; j <- 0L; out <- list()
  for (k in seq_along(aa)) {
    if (aa[k]!="-") i <- i+1L
    if (bb[k]!="-") j <- j+1L
    if (aa[k]!=bb[k]) out[[length(out)+1L]] <- data.frame(
      IMGT_pos_1=if(aa[k]=="-") NA_integer_ else i,
      IMGT_pos_2=if(bb[k]=="-") NA_integer_ else j,
      base_1=aa[k],base_2=bb[k],
      type=if(aa[k]=="-" || bb[k]=="-") "indel" else "substitution")
  }
  if (!length(out)) return(data.frame())
  do.call(rbind,out)
}
# Render each alignment as HTML with visible mismatch and gap highlights.
html_base <- function(x, y) {
  if (x == "-" || y == "-")
    return(paste0('<span class="aln-gap">', x, '</span>'))
  if (x != y)
    return(paste0('<span class="aln-mismatch">', x, '</span>'))
  paste0('<span class="aln-match">', x, '</span>')
}
alignment_blocks <- function(aln, width=75L) {
  a <- chars(pwalign::pattern(aln))
  b <- chars(pwalign::subject(aln))
  blocks <- character()
  for (start in seq.int(1L,length(a),by=width)) {
    end <- min(start+width-1L,length(a))
    ix <- start:end
    mid <- ifelse(a[ix]==b[ix] & a[ix]!="-","|"," ")
    top <- paste0(mapply(html_base,a[ix],b[ix],USE.NAMES=FALSE),collapse="")
    bot <- paste0(mapply(html_base,b[ix],a[ix],USE.NAMES=FALSE),collapse="")
    blocks <- c(blocks,paste0(
      "Contig  ",top,"\n",
      "        ",paste(mid,collapse=""),"\n",
      "IMGT    ",bot))
  }
  paste0('<pre class="tcr-alignment"><code>',
         paste(blocks,collapse="\n\n"),
         '</code></pre>')
}
site_parts <- list()
summary_parts <- list()
alignment_parts <- list()
for (i in seq_len(nrow(spec))) {
  sp <- spec[i,]
  candidates <- grep(paste0("^",sp$gene,"\\*"),names(refs),value=TRUE)
  if (length(candidates)!=2L)
    stop("Expected exactly two IMGT alleles for ",sp$gene)
  contig_id <- if (sp$chain=="TRA")
    x$TRA_contig_id[x$TCR_ID==sp$TCR_ID] else
    x$TRB_contig_id[x$TCR_ID==sp$TCR_ID]
  contig <- unname(seq_by_id[contig_id])
  diff <- reference_diffs(refs[[candidates[1]]],refs[[candidates[2]]])
  aln1 <- align_nt(contig,refs[[candidates[1]]])
  aln2 <- align_nt(contig,refs[[candidates[2]]])
  map1 <- reference_map(aln1,refs[[candidates[1]]])
  sub <- diff[diff$type=="substitution",,drop=FALSE]
  rows <- list()
  for (k in seq_len(nrow(sub))) {
    d <- sub[k,]
    match_row <- map1[map1$ref_pos==d$IMGT_pos_1,,drop=FALSE]
    observed <- if (nrow(match_row)==1L) match_row$observed[1] else NA_character_
    verdict <- if (is.na(observed) || observed=="-") "not covered" else
      if (observed==d$base_1) candidates[1] else
      if (observed==d$base_2) candidates[2] else "other / mismatch"
    rows[[k]] <- data.frame(
      TCR_ID=sp$TCR_ID,chain=sp$chain,gene=sp$gene,
      contig_id=contig_id,
      allele_1=candidates[1],allele_2=candidates[2],
      IMGT_pos_1=d$IMGT_pos_1,IMGT_pos_2=d$IMGT_pos_2,
      allele_1_base=d$base_1,allele_2_base=d$base_2,
      observed_contig_base=if(is.na(observed)) "NA" else observed,
      supports=verdict,stringsAsFactors=FALSE)
  }
  if (length(rows)) site_parts[[length(site_parts)+1L]] <- do.call(rbind,rows)
  verdicts <- if (length(rows)) vapply(rows,function(z) z$supports,character(1)) else character()
  n1 <- sum(verdicts==candidates[1])
  n2 <- sum(verdicts==candidates[2])
  other <- sum(verdicts %in% c("not covered","other / mismatch"))
  favored <- if(n1>0 && n2==0 && other==0) candidates[1] else
    if(n2>0 && n1==0 && other==0) candidates[2] else "Unresolved / partial"
  summary_parts[[length(summary_parts)+1L]] <- data.frame(
    TCR_ID=sp$TCR_ID,chain=sp$chain,gene=sp$gene,
    allele_1=candidates[1],allele_2=candidates[2],
    sites_supporting_1=n1,sites_supporting_2=n2,
    missing_or_other=other, favored_allele=favored,
    indel_differences=sum(diff$type=="indel"),stringsAsFactors=FALSE)
  alignment_parts[[length(alignment_parts)+1L]] <- list(
    TCR_ID=sp$TCR_ID,chain=sp$chain,gene=sp$gene,
    contig_id=contig_id,alleles=candidates,
    alignments=list(aln1,aln2))
}
site_table <- if(length(site_parts)) do.call(rbind,site_parts) else data.frame()
allele_summary <- do.call(rbind,summary_parts)
write.csv(site_table,"TCR9_IMGT_contig_alignment_sites.csv",row.names=FALSE)
write.csv(allele_summary,"TCR9_IMGT_alignment_summary.csv",row.names=FALSE)
```

### Table 1. Allele-resolution summary

Each row compares two IMGT alleles against the representative contig. **Supporting sites are nucleotide positions, not read counts.** An allele preference is provisional and does not establish the donor's germline genotype.

```{r}
knitr::kable(allele_summary,row.names=FALSE)
```

### Table 2. Actual allele-discriminating nucleotide positions

The IMGT positions refer to the respective **reference alleles**, not contig coordinates. `observed_contig_base` comes from the contig-to-IMGT alignment. Indels are counted separately and are **not** used for an automatic allele call.

```{r}
if(nrow(site_table)) knitr::kable(site_table,row.names=FALSE)
```

### Actual IMGT-to-contig alignments (each candidate allele)

<div class="aln-legend"><strong>Color key:</strong>
<span class="aln-mismatch" style="background:#ffd18b;color:#702f00">Orange: mismatch</span>
<span class="aln-gap" style="background:#f7a8bb;color:#7b1027">Pink: insertion/deletion gap (–)</span>
<span class="aln-match" style="color:#146c43">Green: match</span>.
Compare the two candidate allele alignments for each TCR.</div>

Below, `|` marks identical aligned nucleotides. Gaps are shown as `-`. These are **computed alignments**, not illustrative examples. Because the reference is a V or J gene segment, only the matching portion of the assembled contig appears in each local alignment.

```{r results='asis'}
for (entry in alignment_parts) {
  cat("\n\n#### TCR ",entry$TCR_ID," — ",entry$chain," — ",
      entry$gene,"\n\n",sep="")
  cat("Observed FASTA contig: `",entry$contig_id,"`\n\n",sep="")
  for (k in 1:2) {
    cat("**IMGT ",entry$alleles[k]," versus observed contig**\n\n",sep="")
    cat(alignment_blocks(entry$alignments[[k]]),"\n\n",sep="")
  }
}
```

**Antigen-contacting loops:** A nucleotide allele difference does not automatically mean an amino acid change. For variants affecting CDR1/CDR2, the coding frame and translated amino acids must be checked separately. These alignments establish **nucleotide-level evidence only**, not a verified CDR amino-acid assignment.
